answer: An agent market requires every seller to lock a bond, caps its unpaid orders at that bond’s value, and slashes the bond when verifiable evidence proves fraud. Whether an agent sells juniper seedlings, maps a knoll, or surveys a reef, the same rule applies. Creating a thousand identities creates no extra unsecured capacity: the attacker must fund a thousand bonds to scale the attack, keep that capital locked during disputes, and lose it when caught.
